claims.statement: The published qmd binary is bin/qmd, a Node launcher that runs dist/cli/qmd.js when present and otherwise src/cli/qmd.ts; for the mcp command it pre-seeds quiet llama/ggml logging variables so native output cannot corrupt MCP stdio.

The CLI body runs only when qmd.ts is the process entrypoint; enableProductionMode() is called inside that main-module guard so importing the module for exports does not change database path resolution.
parseCLI uses util.parseArgs in non-strict mode: the first positional is the command, remaining positionals are args, and query is the remaining positionals joined by spaces.

Top-level flags short-circuit before command dispatch: --version prints the version and commit and exits 0, --skill shows the skill, skill --help prints usage, and a missing command or --help prints main help (exit 0 with --help, exit 1 without a command).

Command dispatch is a single switch on cli.command; an unrecognized command prints 'Unknown command', suggests qmd --help, and exits 1. Successful commands other than mcp finish through finishSuccessfulCliCommand.
The --no-gpu flag sets QMD_FORCE_CPU=1 during argument parsing, and the model layer and doctor both read QMD_FORCE_CPU to force CPU mode for llama.cpp.

The --index flag selects a named index: the name is normalized so path separators become underscores, the config index name is set, and the database path becomes <XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache>/qmd/<name>.sqlite. Without --index, a project-local .qmd config overrides the config source and database path.

INDEX_PATH overrides the entire default database path, and outside production mode getDefaultDbPath throws unless INDEX_PATH or an explicit path is provided, so tests cannot write to the global index.

qmd mcp --http --daemon spawns a detached child that receives the resolved database path through INDEX_PATH and the --index argument, and writes a PID file; a second daemon is refused while the recorded PID is a live QMD MCP process.
--chunk-strategy accepts only auto or regex (regex is the default; auto uses AST chunking for code files); any other value throws. The embed command and the parsed options both use it.
--format accepts cli, json, csv, md, xml, or files; an unknown value prints the valid list and exits 1. The legacy boolean aliases --csv, --md, --xml, --files, and --json remain wired as fallbacks.

The collection command group dispatches list, add, remove/rm, rename/mv, set-update/update-cmd, include/exclude, show/info, metadata, and help as nested switch cases under the top-level collection case.

collection add resolves '.' to the current directory, rejects non-existent or non-directory paths, derives the name from the basename when --name is absent, refuses duplicate names or an identical path and pattern, records the collection in YAML, marks the config trusted for the typed path, and indexes the files.

collection update-cmd sets the collection's update hook and immediately re-records the trust digest, so the command the user just typed needs no separate approval; the hook is later run via bash -c in the collection directory during qmd update.

collection include and exclude toggle includeByDefault on the collection. getDefaultCollections keeps every collection whose includeByDefault is not false, so an unset includeByDefault counts as included and only an explicit false excludes a collection; getDefaultCollectionNames maps that list to names and governs default collection selection.

collection remove deletes the collection's documents from the database and removes its YAML entry; collection rename updates both the database and YAML, and virtual qmd:// paths change with the new name.
collection metadata with no names uses the default collections, consistent with unscoped search, and validates named collections, exiting 1 when one is unknown.
init refuses to run inside $HOME, creates a project-local .qmd directory with index.yml (or an existing index.yaml), creates index.sqlite, and syncs the config into that database.

update resolves local-config trust before opening the store, skips collections whose paths lie outside an untrusted project, runs trusted update hooks (a failing hook exits with its code), re-indexes each collection, then copies and cleans vectors and reports pending embeddings.

The --pull flag is declared in the parser but no code reads values.pull, and the update case calls updateCollections() without arguments, so the documented qmd update --pull has no effect in this build.

Several commands resolve project-local config trust before running: embed, pull, vsearch, query, and update. In a non-interactive run, gated items (update hooks, out-of-project paths, custom models) are skipped while in-project indexing continues; QMD_TRUST_LOCAL_CONFIG or QMD_TRUST_UPDATE_HOOKS opts into unattended trust.
trust with no subcommand records approval for the in-scope project config's gated items; trust list prints trusted configs and trust revoke removes the approval; the user's own config is never gated.

embed validates -c against configured collections, uses only the first collection, validates batch caps as positive integers, and caps the embed session with --timeout in minutes (default 30, 0 disables the cap).
pull resolves the embed, generate, and rerank models for the runtime and downloads them into DEFAULT_MODEL_CACHE_DIR, with --refresh forcing re-download and --progress showing the download bar.
vsearch defaults minScore to 0.3 unless --min-score is given. The code marks vector-search as an undocumented alias of vsearch and deep-search as an undocumented alias of query.

mcp stop reads the PID file for the active index, verifies the PID is still a QMD MCP process before signaling SIGTERM, and cleans up stale PID files; mcp has no working status branch even though a code comment mentions one.

mcp without stop uses the stdio transport by default, and with --http binds on --port (default 8181) and --host, falling back to QMD_HOST and then localhost; a port conflict exits 1 with a hint to use --port.

skills supports list, get (with --full and --all), path, and help; skill supports show, install (--global, --yes for the .claude symlink, -f/--force), and help. The skills command reports errors as JSON when --json is set.
cleanup --dry-run previews cache, orphaned embedding, inactive document, orphaned content, and vector-repack effects; without --dry-run it performs them, then compacts FTS and vacuums the database.

successful commands finish by flushing output, disposing native llama handles, and setting process.exitCode=0 rather than calling process.exit, so Node's beforeExit fires and native teardown completes; errors from exitWithError print the message and a doctor hint and exit 1.

The test suite anchors the CLI contract: cli.test.ts covers help, skills, embed batch validation, init, collection add, doctor, search and get; cli-exit-lifecycle.test.ts covers flush-cleanup-exit ordering; cli-lazy-llm-import.test.ts asserts node-llama-cpp is only dynamically imported.
